limits.unresolved_targets: A by-name reference names its target in one of three ways. 35,363 hold it in a PlayMaker global and are attributed to the one object that global's writers fill it with (`globals`). 316 set it directly and leave it empty: nothing fills those at run time and the action does nothing, so they are counted and not attributed. 10,956 hold it in the FSM's own variable, which actions fill at run time - a cached reference such as 'The Grid' or 'Plan Management' - and are recovered from which FSM declares the named variable: 1,181 because exactly one does, 1,659 by the variable's type and 3,899 because the holding variable's name picks one out. 4,173 stay ambiguous, recorded as possible where a container is among the candidates, and 44 name a variable no FSM declares. 'attribution' shows how the references kept for each container were tied to it.

fields.name: DAY
fields.label: DAY
fields.explanation: Which day of the run you are on. A new profile starts at 0 and the start of each day adds one, so a save holds the day just played. Almost everything that changes over a run reads it: the draft, which in the early days adjusts which rooms are in the pool and the odds of drawing them; day rules in rooms (the Bedroom's trunk from day 2, a new player's Closet on day 1 always holding one of its special items - the Shovel, the Metal Detector and the like - where on other days it is a coin toss between those and an Ivory Die, a key or a gem, no dirt piles in the Cloister before day 4 unless you have opened its gate or drafted the Root Cellar that day, the Billiard Room's dartboard prizes after days 7 and 21, the Commissary's sale on days 20 and 21, the Kitchen's cupcake on 28 January in each of the run's first five years - in the second year on 1 January instead - the Boudoir's Christmas tree on Christmas Day in the run's first three years and on Christmas Eve in the next two, the Dining Room's dish of the day, Key 8 in the Lost & Found from day 365, the Shelter's time-locked safe, the Apple Orchard's sundial lighting faster from day 7 for a veteran, two Laboratory experiments held back through day 7 for a new player); the estate computer's payroll week, its office emails (new ones after days 16 and 30) and its staff announcements (counted from the day the satellite dish went up); the dates on the packing slip of a package delivered to the Entrance Hall or the Mail Room, on the payroll slip in the Maid's Chamber or the Servant's Quarters, on the drafting note in the Drafting Studio and on the desk in the Vault; the day-end summary; and your blueprint, whose row of keys, gems and gold shows from day 3 even before you have any.

fields.name: Parlor Score
fields.label: Parlor Score
fields.explanation: How well you have been doing at the Parlor, and the only thing that decides which of the four puzzle lists a day's puzzle comes from. It moves by how long you take as well as whether you are right, so answering quickly and correctly is what raises it. A new profile starts at -4, on the A list, and works up as the score climbs. Each list was shuffled once for this profile and does not change. Running one out does not clear it or any other: the Parlor hands on to another list that still has puzzles. A hands on to B, B to C and C to D; D, being the last, goes back to C, then B, then A. So reaching D early and running it out puts you back on whatever you left unfinished. Only when all four are used up does every position start over.

fields.name: SPIRALofSTARS
fields.label: SPIRALofSTARS
fields.explanation: How many words the Spiral of Stars has. It is a constellation of 100 stars in the night sky seen through the Observatory's telescope, there once you have 100 stars, and this stays 0 until then. Nothing ever lowers it. The first time you look through an Observatory's telescope - each Observatory you draft has its own - with it in the sky, a word is added and counted here, even if you never click it. Clicking the constellation shows its description, whose [[sentence|Add a word to Spiral of Stars, then gain one key and one gem for each rank reached, then lose three steps for each rank reached, then gain one coin for each day spent, and then lose two stars. If you have less than forty steps, gain one random item from the showroom. If you have less than twenty steps, open all antechamber doors, then set your steps to forty. Also, your luck has been increased and you can no longer gain steps or gems or keys or gold and your day will immediately end if you ever attempt to add another word to Spiral of Stars.]] grows by that word, and [[does what the words so far say|By how many words there are: nothing up to 3. 4 to 6: gain a key. 7 to 9: a key and a gem. 10: ten keys and ten gems. From 11: a key and a gem for each rank reached that day instead; from 15 also lose 3 steps, at 18 lose 30, and from 19 lose 3 for each rank reached. From 23 also gain a coin, and from 26 a coin for each day. From 32 also lose 2 stars. From 43, with fewer than 40 steps, also gain an item: a random one at 43 to 45, a Showroom luxury item you do not have from 46. From 57, with fewer than 20 steps, all the Antechamber doors open. From 63 your steps are then set to 40, and from 69 your luck rises. From 76 you can gain no more steps that day, from 78 no more gems, from 80 no more keys and from 82 no more gold. At 88 your day ends when you leave the sky; from 89 to 99 it does not, and from 100 on it does again.]], one clause after another. The count keeps going past 100.

From 11 down, stairs appear in the fountain, leading down into the well; at 0 the well is dry, and you can go down to its bottom and reach the basement door. [[Except on a morning at exactly 9|A day that starts with the level at exactly 9 shows the fountain full, as at 12, with its gate shut and no stairs, until the Pump Room changes the level that day. fields.name: lockpicking skill
fields.label: lockpicking skill
fields.explanation:
How much the Laboratory's experiments have improved your lockpicking. It starts at 0, and each such reward ("Your skill in picking locks has improved.") adds one, with no limit. [[It adds to your chance of picking a lock|Lock Pick Kit: the chance starts at 54 in 101, falling to 35 after the day's first successful pick, 30 after the second and 19 after the third.
The skill adds: up to 20, the skill divided by 1.5, rounded up (14 at 20); from 21 to 80, 15 plus a third of the skill over 20, rounded up (35 at 80); above 80, 35 plus a fifth of the skill over 80, rounded up, with the chance at most 98 in 101. The Kit reaches 98 at skill 121 until the day's first success, then 216, 241 and 296.
Pick Sound Amplifier: 90, 85, 70 and then 65 in 101, with the same bonus up to 80 and no further step or limit, so from 101 in 101 it always works: at skill 16 until the day's first success, then 21, 66 and 81.
The Kit also keeps a tally for the day, one up for each failure and one down for each success. At 3 the next pick always works, and, while the skill is 20 or less, at -2 the next one always fails. A forced pick sets the tally to 0 and then counts itself, so it ends at -1 after a forced success and 1 after a forced failure.]].

fields.name: DARE MODE
fields.label: DARE MODE
fields.explanation: Whether this profile is a Dare mode run, chosen on the Mode Selection screen when the profile is started and kept for good. It changes much of the game, for example: eight dares are dealt at the start and one more comes into play each day, up to four, listed on the dare letter in the Entrance Hall and on the blueprint; the first four days are titled "Dare One" to "Dare 4"; breaking a dare is game over; and Room 46 opens only once four dares are in play and all of them are kept that day. [[It also changes a few other things|Each morning in the mode counts you as a veteran player (`_Veteran Player`), which lifts some hidden restrictions earlier - on drafting, the estate computer's upgrades, the items you find and the Laboratory's experiments; the Entrance Hall's doors are open before you take the blueprint; and you never dig up the scraps of paper with contraption recipes - that dig gives coins instead.]]

fields.name: Foundation Elevator Down
fields.label: Foundation Elevator Down
fields.explanation: Whether you have pulled the lever that brings the Foundation's elevator into use. When you first draft the Foundation its elevator is out of reach. The lever is at the Foundation's north end (north as the Room Directory draws its floorplan, so it turns with the room), and the Foundation has no door there: you reach it through a room drafted against that end, with a door on the Foundation's side. Pulling it brings the elevator down to where you can use it - not all the way to the Basement - and from then on you can ride it down to the Basement and back up as you like; it never goes back out of reach, and this stays set for good. It also changes the draft. Until it is set, each day of the first week the Battery Pack has a 60% chance of being kept from turning up (unless you are a veteran player, `_Veteran Player`, or have reached Room 46, `Room 46 Reached`). Once it is set, each morning makes the Master Bedroom Standard and the Billiard Room Unusual, and once you have also drafted three outer rooms, the Tomb turns up far more often among the outer rooms.

fields.name: OFFICE MAIL
fields.label: OFFICE MAIL
fields.explanation: Whether OFFICE MAILBOX is ON on the BLACKBRIDGE ELECTRONIC MAIL SETTINGS screen; it starts ON. Each of the four mailboxes holds different e-mails, and each can only be read at its own room's terminal. With it ON, opening e-mail at the Office's terminal shows the Office's e-mails; with it OFF, the Office's terminal says it has no permission to access e-mail. fields.explanation:
Whether the angel wall in the Tomb has been opened: lowering the angels' arms in the correct order opens it, onto the Catacombs. There, the Draxus statue opens a door that connects the Catacombs with the abandoned mine and, beyond it, the Reservoir. The wall stays open for good, and [[the estate computer's choice of upgrades|Which room a disk offers: this field makes no difference for a veteran player (`_Veteran Player`), or if you have never drafted the Cloister. Otherwise, while the Cloister has no upgrade, an open angel wall adds about 10% to the chance that a disk offers it; once the Cloister has its upgrade, that extra chance goes to the first of the Parlor, Aquarium and Mail Room without one.
Which upgrades the Cloister offers: once the angel wall is open and you have 12 stars or more, the Cloister of Draxus gets a chance, up to 30%, of being among them. Having drafted the Throne Room more than five times takes that chance away, unless you are a veteran player.
Whatever this field says, the Cloister of Draxus is always among them on a day the Draxus constellation is active.]] checks it.

fields.name: the curse of black bridge
fields.label: the curse of black bridge
fields.explanation: Whether you have bought The Curse of Black Bridge at the Bookshop, which sells each book once. Buying it does not hand you the book: it adds it to the Library's request form, and the Library has it once you ask for it, and it is one of [[five books|History of Orindia (first edition), A New Clue, Drafting Strategy volumes 4 and 5, and The Curse of Black Bridge. Drafting from a Library door, the floorplan in slot 3 can be the Bookshop once the Library has been drafted more than seven times, or more than four with `_Veteran Player` or `Room 46 Reached` set. Until you have drafted the Bookshop twice it is an even chance; after that it depends on how many of the five you have bought: 60% with none or one, 50% with two to four, and 10% with all five. A Hall Pass in hand sets the count aside and keeps it at 60%. With `_Veteran Player` or `Room 46 Reached` set, it also gives the Bookshop a 90% roll first, and a miss gets a second try at the odds above. Library doors offer it at most once a day: once offered, it is not offered again that day, even if you did not take it.]] whose count sets how often a Library door offers the Bookshop: the more of them you have bought, the less often.

fields.explanation: How many times you have drafted each room. A new profile starts every room at 0 except the Entrance Hall, the Antechamber and Room 46, which start at 1, and while the Foundation stands its count is set back to 1 every morning. fields.name: save_created
fields.label: save_created
fields.explanation: When the save system first stamped this file, and unchanged afterwards. That is the creation date only for a save made under the current system: a save carried over from an older one that did not hold this field gets stamped at the moment of conversion instead, so it can be much later than when the player actually started. Treat it as 'created or converted', not as the start of the run.

fields.name: data_last_modified
fields.label: data_last_modified
fields.explanation: When the game last wrote this file. On a file the game itself wrote, this matches the file's own modification date on disk to the second; if the two disagree, something other than the game put the file there, such as a copy or a cloud sync.

fields.name: game_version
fields.label: game_version
fields.explanation: The build of the game that wrote this file. It is an internal build id and does not resemble the version in the patch notes, which are numbered differently. It matters because the explanations shown here were extracted from one particular build: if the two do not agree, the labels may no longer fit this save.

fields.name: save_system_version
fields.label: save_system_version
fields.explanation: Which revision of the save layout this file uses. It does change between versions of the game: an older revision may not carry every block a newer one does, and a save old enough has no SaveFileInfo block at all, so it records neither the build nor these dates.
